title: Load testing, SLOs and capacity planning
goal: Measure the laptop fleet with k6 (streaming), find the knee of the latency/throughput curve, set SLOs for TTFT p95 and TPOT p95, compute cost per 1M tokens on the laptop, and extrapolate to a GPU fleet for a frontier-size open model, naming every assumption.

changes.note: Streaming chat helper: TTFT from time-to-first-byte, TPOT from receive time / (tokens − 1), output token counter.
Constant arrival rate (open model) at RATE; SLO thresholds; one JSON summary line.
Break-it: long prompts flood the replicas while short chats measure TTFT.
Break-it: the free tenant floods while gold measures TTFT.
Runs step.js at increasing rates and prints one row per rate.
Laptop cost per 1M tokens and GPU fleet sizing for Llama 3.1 70B or 405B, every input a named assumption.
A gold tenant with a budget no test reaches.
k6 service in the loadtest profile.
Optional NVIDIA override: CUDA build, all layers on the GPU.

run.label: Smoke test (local k6, or the container)
run.cmd: k6 run k6/smoke.js || docker compose --profile loadtest run --rm k6 run /scripts/smoke.js

run.label: Cost and fleet arithmetic with your number

verify.label: Smoke passes
verify.expect: checks 100%, http_req_failed 0.00%, thresholds marked as passed, and ttft / tpot trends in the summary.

verify.label: The knee table
verify.expect: One row per rate: at low rates TTFT p95 stays near your stage 1 baseline and fail% is 0; past the knee TTFT p95 jumps (queueing), then fail% rises (shedding) while out_tok/s stops growing. Mark the last rate where all three SLO thresholds hold.

verify.label: Capacity arithmetic
verify.expect: With 40 tokens/s, 30 W and $0.15/kWh: energy $0.031 per 1M output tokens, hardware amortisation $1.19, total $1.22. Then rerun with your own knee number.

verify.label: Frontier fleet
verify.expect: Llama 3.1 70B, FP8 weights, TP=2, defaults: 65.4 GB of KV memory per replica (199,585 tokens), TPOT 28.0 ms at batch 64, 2,286 output tokens/s per replica, 318 GPUs at a 200,000 tokens/s peak (398 with headroom), $1.10 per 1M output tokens at $2.50/GPU-hour.

concepts.how: The same back-of-envelope method as any design, now with tokens: demand, per-unit capacity, units, headroom.
Capacity planning end to end: memory, latency-bound batch size, prefill check, headroom.
The roofline: decode reads all weights and KV per step, so bandwidth sets TPOT.
Continuous batching, paged attention, prefix caching, chunked prefill, disaggregated prefill/decode: what changes the numbers.
Cuts TPOT when draft tokens are usually accepted; an option once decode, not prefill, is the bottleneck.
Tensor parallelism splits each layer across GPUs (TP in the calculator); pipeline parallelism splits layers.
TTFT p95 < 2 s and TPOT p95 < 200 ms as the lab SLOs; the knee is where the error budget starts burning.
Present the plan as a reviewer would want it: the number, the assumptions behind it, and which assumption it is most sensitive to.
Capacity is the deep dive interviewers push on for LLM serving: KV memory, batch size versus TPOT, prefill versus decode.

checkpoints.text: k6 smoke passed with TTFT and TPOT trends in the summary.
I ran find-knee.sh and marked the highest rate that met all SLO thresholds.
I computed my laptop's cost per 1M output tokens with my own knee number.
I changed one assumption in capacity.mjs (TP, FP8 KV, batch, prefix hit rate) and explained how the GPU count moved.
I compared my stage 0 design with what I built and the model answer.
